name: Neutralisation of hydrochloric acid by sodium hydroxide

enthalpy_kj_per_mol.source: Educational classroom approximation used for the simulation

observations.heat: The mixture warms up because neutralisation releases heat.
observations.neutral: The acid and base have exactly cancelled: the mixture is neutral (pH 7).
observations.acidic: There is more acid than base, so the mixture is still acidic.
observations.basic: There is more base than acid, so the mixture is still basic.

explanation: Hydrogen ions from the acid and hydroxide ions from the base combine to form water, leaving a dissolved salt behind.
